# Tutorial section reference

`outline.json` retains second-level section headings from diffraction-lib's committed
Python tutorial sources. Every entry records its source Git blob and SHA-256; the common
reference commit identifies the tree in which those blobs were found. Material without
an exact reference uses the closest tutorial of the same technique. This checks structure,
not agreement of scientific output or successful execution on Colab.

`bank.py REPOSITORY COMMIT OUTPUT NAME=BLOB ...` regenerates this outline from an
independently supplied checkout. It reads source blobs, not edi notebooks. Section matching
ignores letter case; extra edi sections are allowed, and reference sections keep their order.
A documented structural departure needs an explicit reviewed update to the mapping.

The active notebook chapter gate reads `current.json` and retains the published sections in order,
with the declared empty-project-first adaptation. Co₂SiO₄ on HEiDi follows the independently
captured single-crystal HEiDi outline at the common pinned upstream commit; its entry records
blob `f053dbedcfaccd8f75c25e4d24c24006c412374f` and the source-byte SHA-256. This is a teaching
outline reference and makes no claim about numerical output. Notebook execution remains a
separate requirement.

Owner correction 7101f0fd9 (2026-11-09) withdraws exact upstream fit-cycle matching
and its prose-deviation exemption. The captured `stages.json` remains an external
physics/teaching reference, including the previously required correlation lessons.
Edi's own cumulative fitting strategy governs stage admission: alignment first,
one new scientific block per fit, accepted independent parameters kept free, and
no fixed/free reset or re-release. The hidden strategy observer uses the skill's
committed blob 555b7725370d7ea55c8daa6ba0084916dc5ee514 and the owner correction,
not values or plans generated by the implementation. Constraint dependents may be
fixed while their accepted independent partners stay free. 'A few' individual
members means at most three per group per stage in the collective-action guard;
three/four/fourteen controls exercise both sides for fixing and freeing.
